messages:
nate: Running `redwoodctl localserve` inside a dev container. localserve starts but auth handshake fails: `auth: retrying` and `device busy`. The host has redwood auth-agent running too. Anyone understand how localserve expects the auth socket to be shared?

sophie: Are you bind-mounting /run/user/1000 or the token socket into the container? We require the token socket to be accessible. If both host and container auth-agents try to claim the same socket you'll get device busy.

nate: I mounted /run/user/1000/redwood.token into /run/redwood/token in the container and set REDWOOD_TOKEN_PATH to that path. It still shows two agents in ps.

rahul: If the host has agent auto-start via systemd or shell init, you'll end up with duplicate agents. Best practice: run localserve with `--no-auth-agent` in container and point to host token file read-only, or disable host agent for the session: `systemctl --user stop redwood-auth || true`.

sophie: We should add a clearer note in the DX guide about container workflows: explain token path mounting, recommended --no-auth-agent flag, and the race condition. Also consider adding a container-friendly mode that uses file-based lock instead of exclusive device to avoid device busy.

nate: Workaround worked: stopped host agent and started container localserve with `--no-auth-agent`. Filed a small PR to the sample devcontainer with recommended mounts and envs.

devex-bot: Created DX ticket DX-5108: "localdev: docs for running localserve in containers, handle token socket races, add --no-auth-agent option to help output."
